model: Gemma4 26B A4B TL2 rotated, PR #4428 HTP fused profile
scope: Same-model-process explicit DSP INT8 checkpoints. Not CPU Flash, automatic radix/LRU tiering, or cross-process persistence.
protocol: Model weights and graph are warmed before measured trials.
Initial prompt N-2 tokens produces two output IDs. Checkpoint contains N-1 committed KV rows and one pending feedback token.
Recomputation prefills exactly the same N token IDs (original prompt + generated IDs). The benchmark verifies tokenization round trip before comparing.
DRAM and restored runs consume the pending feedback token with no additional user tokens; first emitted-token TTFT is measured.
Cold restore fsyncs the checkpoint and requests per-file FADV_DONTNEED before timing. /proc/self/io proves storage reads at least the whole checkpoint size.
restore_ms includes file I/O, checksum, RPC transfer, DSP allocation/import and atomic commit. restore_plus_ttft includes that plus the resumed request TTFT.
Export is completed before park frees all device K/V allocations. Scales and decode scratch remain allocated in the parked context.
Save+sync+restore+TTFT includes observed checkpoint export/park and fsync/advice preparation, excluding the original seed computation.
Resident versus restored output IDs and committed positions must match exactly. Recomputed output IDs are recorded separately: rebuilding can recalibrate INT8 scales.
Mode order and recomputation order alternate by repetition. Expert-cache contents may evolve between paths; CPU/device clocks are not locked. Three samples are exploratory.
At 4096 the initial prompt includes an assistant-turn delimiter so generated text cannot merge into preceding text on re-tokenization. Input IDs are retained.
binary_revision_note: Cases 128/512/1024 use measured-binary-sha256. Case 4096 and the functional check use final-device-sha256, adding host snapshot API rejection guards and a tokenizer-safe assistant delimiter for the 4096 benchmark. The DSP checkpoint implementation and attention arithmetic are the same.
